_about: Criterion dictionary for tools/wem_lint.py — the controlled vocabulary of CODE
IDENTIFIERS the NFR lint measures src/wattleflow against (NFR-ORG-01/02/03,
NFR-SEC-03). This file is the criterion of the `wattleflow-workflow` (clean
core) distribution; `wattleflow-processors` carries its own next to its tools/.
JSON, not YAML: the lint is stdlib-only by design (no PyYAML dependency) and
json is the only structured format the standard library parses. Keys starting
with an underscore are prose and are dropped by the loader.
Converted from the `code:` block of documentation/dictionary.yaml on 2026-07-29
and translated to UK English. The Croatian dictionary.yaml stays the source of
truth for the DISCOURSE vocabulary (entries + acronyms) and is no longer read
by this tool.
PRESENTATION LIVES ELSEWHERE (since 2026-07-31): report strings and the finding
catalogue moved to tools/messages.json, shared by every distribution. This file
may still carry inline MESSAGES / CATALOGUE keys — they would win — but it does
not, so a wording fix never touches a criterion version.
WARNING — the discourse `acronyms` table and `identifier_acronyms` below are
NOT the same vocabulary and must not be merged: the former holds doctrine
abbreviations (DQI, NFR, PDSA, SBVR) read by people, the latter holds tokens
appearing in code identifiers (JSON, URI, SQL, OSCAL) read by the lint. Their
intersection is empty (measured 2026-07-28) and must stay empty — merging them
would make one sign carry two roles.
Versioning: `criterion_version` versions THIS criterion, `dictionary_version`
names the discourse registry revision it was cut from. They are deliberately
separate — editing an entry must not invalidate a code conformance snapshot,
nor the reverse (reproducibility triple).
Governance: every extension — a new domain, base family, acronym or TypeVar
role — requires a DR record, never an ad-hoc edit.
_criterion_version: v0.0.0.93). Names only, no rule semantics: vectors stay comparable with 0.8.0.
0.8.0 (2026-07-31) — rule semantics changed, so old and new vectors are not
comparable without a declared note (D-10). Changes, per analysis
(DR-WFL-003 waivers, without which `clean_core_imports` would turn a proven
waiver into an ERROR); absent domains `audit`, `blackboards`, `mappers`
removed (they are not in this tree — `mappers` moved to processors per
NFR-SEC-03); blind spots extended; presentation moved to messages.json.
PENDING: DR-PRC-001 must enact this revision — until then the criterion is a
draft and its findings are conformant, not descriptive (D-08).
_python_reference: Defines the 'stdlib' set for ORG-01; must track requires-python in pyproject.toml.
_acronym_identifier_casing: Enforcement level of the acronym-casing criterion — a registry fact under DR
governance rather than a constant in the tool: `adopted` makes the check an
ERROR, any other status falls back to the severity declared for the
`acronym_case` rule below (single resolution path since v1.11.0).

acronym_identifier_casing.note: the lint warns (WARNING, waiver declared) instead of failing the build until the decision is taken

_blind_spots: Declared unmeasured territory (§5, column 3). Reported as INFO on every run so
the vector can never read as full coverage.
blind_spots: imports inside the shared namespace are not modelled as edges, so cycles and layering within helpers/ are unmeasured (helpers->domain acyclicity and helper fan-in ARE measured)
the ORG-02 name grammar (Subject/Operation) is inert in this distribution: no `subjects` block and no `pipelines` domain are declared, so only criterion 6 (prohibited_standalone) is enforced here
ORG-01 measures the import graph, never the runtime one: dynamic edges (ClassLoader, YAML-declared types) are invisible to the AST, so blast radius per NFR-SEC-01 is under-counted
a strategic adversary is beyond the reach of the lint
_rules: The rule table as the NFR registry declares it: id, requirement, check,
severity and waiver policy. The tool resolves severity from here (POLICY §9),
and reports both directions of drift: a rule declared but not implemented (K7)
and a check emitted but not declared (K8).
_domains: NFR-ORG-01 — top-level functional packages under src/wattleflow. `helpers` is
the shared namespace, NOT a domain: it must not appear here, or intra-helper
imports get misreported as acyclicity breaks. `constants` is likewise absent:
it imports nothing intra-project, so it is foundation material every layer may
src/wattleflow belongs to them (mappers moved to wattleflow-processors per
NFR-SEC-03). The `absent-domain` check (K10) keeps this list honest from now on.
_report_language: Default report language of the lint. UK English is the default and the
fallback (POLICY §3.2); --lang overrides it per run. Presentation, not
criterion (D-13) — the strings themselves live in tools/messages.json.
_scope: Distribution tier. wattleflow-workflow is clean core: stdlib plus the libraries
listed in `core_libraries` only (§7.1). A module importing anything outside
(stdlib ∪ wattleflow ∪ core_libraries) belongs to another distribution and is
skipped by the ORG rules — and, since v1.11.0, REPORTED as a K9 supply-chain
finding (NFR-SEC-03 criterion 1), because a silent skip is what the criterion
`guarded_optional` is the only waiver: modules whose third-party reference sits
behind a try/except branch with a FUNCTIONALLY COMPLETE fallback (DR-WFL-003).
The test is masking (mask the package — the module must still import and work),
never code review; a branch that raises, returns None or degrades is NOT guarded.
`exclude_paths` opts modules out by path glob, for cases the import filter
_distribution_manifest: NFR-SEC-03 criteria 2/3 — the packaging manifest of this distribution, read by
the `distribution_manifest` check (stdlib tomllib). `pyproject` is relative to
the repository root (the parent of tools/).
_bases: NFR-ORG-02 — the inheritance roots of the framework; every concrete name in
the workflow package derives from one of these. Grouped by family: each family
lists its core interface(s) (I*, from wattleflow.core) and its concrete base(s)
(concrete/*). A class belongs to a family if it inherits one of that family's
_capabilities: NFR-ORG-04 — recognised cross-cutting capabilities: callable helpers named by
capability, never specialisations of a domain primitive.
_prohibited_standalone: Bare generic role nouns prohibited as STANDALONE class names (NFR-ORG-02
criterion 6; NFR-ORG-04 criterion 3 delegates its capability role-nouns here).
The same noun is legal as a qualified facet — `DriverS3UriParser`, not `Parser`.
_identifier_acronyms: Acronym TOKENS as they appear in code identifiers — distinct from the discourse `acronyms` table (see the note above).
_type_vars: NFR-ORG-03 — a TypeVar names the SEMANTIC ROLE the type plays in the generic
contract, not the mechanism (the fact that it is a type). Acronym casing is
roles     — the closed controlled vocabulary (criterion 1). `Adaptee` is the
synonyms  — collapsed to a canonical role (criterion 6; the lint flags and suggests)
tolerated — branded names awaiting a DR decision (rename to a canonical role vs
keep): WARNING, not ERROR, until decided — the same tolerance policy
_preset_allowed: NFR-ORG-07 — Preset Whitelist Declaration. A class whose optional runtime
configuration is carried by PresetDecorator declares the permitted keys in a
Why a rule and not a preference: PresetDecorator resolves the whitelist from
the CLASS (`type(parent).ALLOWED`). A declaration under any other name, or at
module scope, is invisible to that resolution — the whitelist reads as empty
and every configuration key the caller passes is dropped WITHOUT ERROR. The
failure is silent by construction, which is why the severity is `error`.
The synonyms below were all in use on 2026-08-01 (27 declarations across 4
spellings) and are recorded so the check can name what it found.
